newsitem.title: UK: ONS invites comments on UK jobs data revamp plans.
newsitem.headline: ONS invites comments on UK jobs data revamp plans.

text.p: The Office for National Statistics is inviting comments on its draft proposals for overhauling official UK unemployment statistics in a bid to improve the credibility of the data.

The ONS said it wanted to give a higher profile to the Labour Force Survey, which conforms to the way the widely recognised International Labour Organisation measures unemployment -- it looks at all those out of work and seeking jobs whether or not they can claim benefit.

At present, the UK's headline measure of unemployment is the seasonally adjusted benefit claimant count which has been pulled downwards by several tightenings of the conditions for claiming benefit such as the introduction of the Job Seeker's Allowance.
Britain's new Labour government had frequently accused the former Conservative government of concealing the true level of unemployment and said it was vital to restore credibility of the data.
The ONS said in a press release that the proposed changes included:
-- The Labour Force Survey to be integrated with other labour market data to form a single monthly press release.
-- Greater prominence for LFS data in line with the government reponse to the select committee on employment's recommendations.
-- Improved presentation of labour market statistics with a clear overview of of key economic indicators.
-- Consistent style to be adopted throughout.
-- Discontinuing the separate quarterly bulletin and expanding the content of Labour Market Trends.
The ONS said it would hold talks with economists, statisticians and the media about how best to present the figures and hoped to bring in any changes by late summer.
